description:
INDIRECT's `a1` flag. The `a1 = FALSE` cases show the R1C1 grammar being read rather than the flag being ignored: `R2C3` resolves to the same cell `C2` names, and the string ADDRESS itself emits under `a1 = FALSE` round trips back through INDIRECT.
The `a1 = TRUE` cases are what make that meaningful. The first shows the reference resolves at all; the second shows Excel rejects R1C1 text when the flag says A1 -- without it, "R2C3 resolved" would not distinguish Excel honouring the flag from Excel ignoring ref_text's syntax entirely. Each style rejects the other's spelling, so the flag selects a grammar instead of adding a fallback.
Relative axes (`R[1]C[-1]`, bare `RC`) are not covered here: they measure from the cell holding the formula, and the harness places every case at a fixed anchor, so a golden would pin the anchor rather than the semantics. Those live in tests/unit/eval/builtins_references_test.cpp.
